# dsh-agent-hints
Per-request serving-intent hints for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): every main-line model request carries a
structured **AgentHint on the `X-Agent-Hint` HTTP header** (UTF-8 JSON, base64url) — session identi
ty, agent status, priority, and cache control — so a serving engine (your inference gateway) can obs
erve and act on what the agent is doing, per the "agent signals, engine consumes" pattern.
The plugin registers an **independent provider route `deepseek-hint`** backed by its own chat-comple
tions adapter. The official `deepseek-official` route stays mounted and remains the fallback; deploy
ment switches via `agent-default-model.provider`. Zero harness source modification, zero harness run
time dependencies (cordis is touched as a structural duck type only).
English | 中文 · Design notes: docs/design.md (中文)
## How it works
The harness `LlmAdapter` contract is thin (only `stream()` is required), and the official adapter co
nstructs its HTTP headers inside its `request()` implementation with no extension point. This plugin
therefore ships a self-contained adapter that implements the contract structurally and adds one hea
refore ships a self-contained adapter that implements the contract structurally and adds one header:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The request body stays in the provider's original chat-completions format and **never carries hint f
ields**. To an endpoint that does not understand the header, it is a harmless unknown header.
This differs from static header-injection approaches (e.g. wrapping `fetch` to set fixed headers lik
e a `user-agent`): here the hint value is **derived per request** from the session's durable event l
og (call index, compaction epoch, last tool result time) and the session lineage — there is nothing
static to configure.
### Header emission rules
- **Main-line requests only**: auxiliary calls (`compaction`, `session-title` purposes) and requests

without a session identity carry no hint.
- `strict_priority` is **never sent** by an agent (truste

d-control-plane field).
- `agent_status` follows the four-value contract. `running` by default; `pau
se` while a tool call is unanswered (every tool call counts as waiting on something external, per th
is deployment's adjudication); `resume` on the first request after the release, one-shot. `finalize`
never rides the header — a completed run has no closing request — it is session-scoped (session ove
r, release session-level resources) and rides the `session/disposed` status event, exactly once per

session lifetime as its last event.
- `priority` is the dynamic two-level value by default: turn-ope
ning requests are user intervention (`3` / `user_waiting`), everything else is self-driven continuat
ion (`1` / `critical_path`). A static `{level, reason}` is a constant override folded into `{1, 3}`;

`null` omits the field.
- `cache_control` is one dynamic `ephemeral` entry by default: `range.end`
is the wire message count and `ttl_s = clamp(last interval × 2, 60, 3600)`. Declarations are suppres
sed for a compaction round, a model/tool-set change, or a prefix below 128 estimated tokens. A stati
c array overrides the policy (ephemeral only, explicit `ttl_s`); an entry without an explicit `range
` declares the request's wire message count (`range.end` + `unit: message`) at send time. `null` omi

ts it.
- `prediction` rides the same header when a source is configured (`predictionTrie` and/or `pr
edictionStatic`); with no source configured the block is omitted and the wire shape is unchanged. Va
lues come from an offline trie (longest tool-sequence-prefix match) with per-field static fallback.
- Session identity mirrors the official adapter: `x-deepseek-harness-session-id` (when a session id
exists) and `x-deepseek-harness-compact: 1` (on compaction) are sent as-is.
### The `X-Agent-Hint` payload

Out-of-band status events (`pause` → `running` → `finalize` per working session, incl. awaited tool
names and call ids) are reported to the optional `statusSink` (local JSONL file); the `emit()` seam
is where a gateway client takes over.

The API key resolves per request: credentials service first (`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` / Models
page), then the environment variable named by `apiKeyEnv` — the same order as the official adapter.
### Configuration reference
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| `baseURL` | string | inherits `$DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` → `https://api.deepseek.com` | Upstream base; e

very chat request posts to `${baseURL}/chat/completions` |
| `apiKeyEnv` | string | inherits `$DEEPS
EEK_API_KEY_ENV` → `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | Environment-variable name resolved per request (credentials

service first) |
| `agentType` | string | `agent` | Reported as `session.agent_type` |
| `priority`
| `"dynamic"`, `{level, reason}`, or `null` | `"dynamic"` | Two-level soft priority. Dynamic: `3`/`u
ser_waiting` on turn-opening requests, `1`/`critical_path` otherwise. A static object is folded into

`{1, 3}`; `null` omits the field |
| `cacheControl` | `"dynamic"`, array, or `null` | `"dynamic"` |
Dynamic: one `ephemeral` entry with a derived TTL. A static array overrides the policy (`ephemeral`
only, explicit `ttl_s`, at most one entry); an entry without `range` declares the request's wire me

ssage count. `null` omits the field |
